reason: The single cited passage (E1) directly supports all key premises: it reports that chemical heterogeneity in CoCrFeNi nanopillars causes wide SFE variations, which coordinate twinning and slip, leading to deformation delocalization and ~110% uniform elongation at 0.6–1.0 GPa. The hypothesis accurately represents this evidence, though the evidence is from nanoscale single crystals, while the hypothesis proposes a bulk-scale test.
premises: Atomic-scale chemical heterogeneity in CoCrFeNi creates wide variations in generalized stacking fault energy.
These SFE variations promote spatial and synergistic coordination of deformation twinning and dislocation slip.
This coordination promotes deformation delocalization and delays necking failure.
The mechanism yields ultrahigh uniform tensile ductility at high flow stress.
